title: CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
chineseTitle: 第 32 章：奎恩学院金榜题名

paragraphs.en: The end of June marked the conclusion of the term and Miss Stacy's tenure at Avonlea school. Anne and Diana walked home that evening, their eyes red from tears, handkerchiefs damp with sobs. Diana looked back at the schoolhouse from the spruce hill, sighing deeply.
paragraphs.zh: 六月底标志着学期和斯泰西小姐在埃文利学校的任期结束。安妮和戴安娜当晚走回家时，眼睛红肿，手帕已被泪水浸湿。戴安娜从云杉山顶回望学校，深深叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: "It feels like everything is ending," she said dejectedly.
paragraphs.zh: 她说得沮丧不已：“感觉一切都要结束了。”

paragraphs.en: Anne tried to console her but found no dry spots on her own handkerchief. "You shouldn't feel as bad as I do," Anne said. "You'll return next winter, but I might never see the dear old school again."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮试图安慰她，但发现自己手帕上已经湿透了。“你不应该像我这么难过，”安妮说，“你明年冬天还会回来的，但我可能再也见不到那亲爱的旧学校了。”

paragraphs.en: Diana agreed, saying it wouldn't be the same without Miss Stacy or their friends. She would sit alone, unable to bear another desk partner after Anne. "We've had such fun times, haven't we, Anne?
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜同意了，说没有斯泰西小姐或朋友们在，确实不一样。她将独自一人坐着，再也忍受不了另一个同桌伙伴。“我们曾经度过了那么多愉快的时光，不是吗，安妮？”

paragraphs.en: It's terrible to think they're over," Diana said, tears rolling down her cheeks.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜说着，泪水顺着脸颊滚落下来，让人感到无比心酸。

paragraphs.en: Anne pleaded, "Stop crying, please. Once I put away my handkerchief, you start again. As Mrs. Lynde says, 'If you can’t be cheerful, be as cheerful as you can.'
paragraphs.zh: 安妮央求道：“别哭了，好吗？我一收起手帕，你就又哭了起来。就像雷切尔·林德夫人说的，‘如果你不能快乐，那就尽量让自己看起来快乐一些。’”

paragraphs.en: I might return next year; these failures are becoming too frequent."
paragraphs.zh: 我或许可以明年再来；这样的失败太频繁了。

paragraphs.en: Diana reminded Anne of her excellent performance in Miss Stacy's exams. "But those weren't the real thing," Anne replied. "Thinking about the actual exam gives me a terrible fluttery feeling.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜提醒安妮她在斯泰西小姐的考试中表现优异。“可那不是真正的考试嘛,” 安妮回答说，“一想到正式的考试，我就感到一阵紧张不安。”

paragraphs.en: And my number is thirteen, which Josie Pye says is unlucky. I'm not superstitious, but it still worries me."
paragraphs.zh: 而我的号码是十三，乔西·派伊说这是一个不吉利的数字。我不信这些迷信的事，但心里还是有些不安。

paragraphs.en: Diana wished she could join Anne for the exams. "Wouldn't we have a perfect time?" Diana said.
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜多想能和安妮一起参加考试啊。“我们俩一起去岂不是再好不过了？”戴安娜说道。

paragraphs.en: "But you'll need to study in the evenings."
paragraphs.zh: “但你晚上还得抽时间学习。”

paragraphs.en: Anne went to town on Monday, and Diana eagerly checked the post office on Wednesday. Anne wrote back that night: "Dearest Diana, I'm writing this in Beechwood's library tonight. Last night, feeling terribly lonely alone in my room, I wished you were there.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮周一去了镇上，戴安娜周三迫不及待地检查了邮局。当晚，安妮回信写道：“最亲爱的戴安娜，我今晚在橡树屋的图书馆里写这封信。昨晚独自一人房间里感到非常孤独，真希望你也在那里。”

paragraphs.en: Despite Miss Stacy's advice against studying, it was hard to resist opening my history book.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管斯泰西小姐劝我不要复习历史，但还是忍不住打开了课本。

paragraphs.en: Miss Stacy picked her up and they went to the Academy, stopping by Jane and Ruby's rooms on their way. Ruby's hands were icy cold, while Josie worried Anne wasn't strong enough for the teacher's course. Even now, Anne didn't feel she'd made much progress in liking Josie Pye.
paragraphs.zh: 斯蒂西小姐一把抱起安妮，她们一起前往学院，在途中还顺道去了简和朱茜的房间。朱茜的手冰凉得吓人，而Josie则担心安妮的身体状况还不足以应对老师的课程。即便如此，安妮自己也觉得对Josie·派伊的好感并没有多少增加。

paragraphs.en: At the Academy, Moody Spurgeon was muttering to himself on the steps, repeating his multiplication table to calm his nerves. When Jane asked what he was doing, he explained that it helped him remember everything."
paragraphs.zh: 在学院里，莫迪·斯普尔根在台阶上自言自语，嘴里重复着乘法表以平复心情。当简问他这是干什么时，他解释说这样做有助于他记住所有内容。

paragraphs.en: When Miss Stacy left us, Jane remained composed, envying her steadiness. My hands trembled as I picked up my English exam sheet. Recalling the moment when I asked Marilla to stay at Green Gables, I felt a mix of anxiety and determination.
paragraphs.zh: 斯蒂西小姐离开后，简依然镇定自若，羡慕她的从容。我颤抖着手拿起英语考试的试卷。回想起请求玛丽拉留在绿山墙农庄的那个瞬间，我的心情交织着焦虑与决心。

paragraphs.en: At noon, we returned home for dinner before heading back for history class in the afternoon. The history paper was challenging, and I struggled with dates. However, I believed I performed reasonably well.
paragraphs.zh: 中午时分，我们回家吃了饭，然后下午又返回学校上历史课。那张历史试卷难度不小，日期记起来有些吃力。不过，我觉得自己表现还算不错。

paragraphs.en: In the evening, I visited other girls. Moody Spurgeon, who had failed history, wandered around dejectedly. I encouraged him to stay until the end, as it would be unfair to Miss Stacy if he left.
paragraphs.zh: 傍晚时分，我去拜访了其他几位女孩。莫迪·斯普尔根因历史课不及格而显得郁郁寡欢，漫无目的地走来走去。我鼓励他坚持到最后，毕竟如果他现在就离开，对史蒂西小姐来说未免有些不公平。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes, I wished I were a boy, but seeing Moody's struggle made me glad I was a girl.
paragraphs.zh: 有时，我真希望是个男孩，但看到莫迪挣扎的样子让我庆幸自己是女孩。

paragraphs.en: Ruby was in tears when we arrived at their boardinghouse; she had found an error in her English paper. We went uptown for ice cream, wishing Diana could have been with us.
paragraphs.zh: 我们抵达她们的寄宿家庭时，鲁比泪眼汪汪；她在英语论文中发现了一个错误。我们上街买了冰淇淋，真希望戴安娜能和我们一起分享这份喜悦。

paragraphs.en: I longed for the geometry exam to be over. Despite Mrs. Lynde’s reminder that life would continue regardless of my performance, I felt uneasy about it.
paragraphs.zh: 我希望几何考试赶快结束。尽管雷切尔·林德夫人提醒我说，无论我的表现如何，生活都会继续下去，但我仍然感到不安。

paragraphs.en: Anne returned to Green Gables on Friday evening, tired but triumphant. Diana greeted her warmly upon arrival.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮周五傍晚回到了绿山墙农庄，虽然疲惫但心情振奋。戴安娜一到便热情地迎接了她。

paragraphs.en: "Anne, darling! It's wonderful to see you back. How did your exams go?"
paragraphs.zh: 安妮，亲爱的！你回来了真是太好了。你的考试怎么样？

paragraphs.en: "Not great in geometry," Anne admitted. "I'm not sure I passed and I feel awful about it."
paragraphs.zh: “几何成绩一般，”安妮承认道，“我也不确定是否通过了，心里挺内疚的。”

paragraphs.en: "But the others?" Diana pressed.
paragraphs.zh: “可是其他人呢？”戴安娜追问。

paragraphs.en: "The girls think they didn't pass, but I believe they did well. Josie says geometry was too easy for a ten-year-old! Moody Spurgeon thinks he failed history, and Charlie believes he missed algebra.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩们认为自己没过，但我相信她们考得不错。乔西说几何对她这个十岁的小孩来说太简单了！莫蒂·斯普尔根觉得自己历史没及格，查理则认为自己错失了代数题。

paragraphs.en: We won’t know anything until the pass list is out in two weeks."
paragraphs.zh: 两周后发榜，我们才能知道结果。

paragraphs.en: Anne wished she could sleep through the suspense.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮巴不得能熬过这段煎熬的等待。

paragraphs.en: Diana reassured her: "You'll do fine, Anne. Don't worry."
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜安慰她说：“安妮，你一定会做得很好。别担心。”

paragraphs.en: But Anne insisted on excelling over Gilbert Blythe. She had competed fiercely during the exams, meeting him several times without acknowledging each other. Each time, she wished they were friends and vowed to outperform him.
paragraphs.zh: 但是安妮坚持要在吉尔伯特·布雷思white头上出类拔萃。她在考试中与他激烈竞争，几次相遇却互不相认。每次见面时，她都希望两人能成为朋友，并发誓要超越他。

paragraphs.en: Everyone in Avonlea wondered who would come first, with Jimmy Glover and Ned Wright even betting on it. Josie Pye was convinced Gilbert would win. Anne feared her failure would be unbearable.
paragraphs.zh: 在埃文利，大家纷纷猜测谁能拔得头筹，吉米·格洛弗和内德·沃特希甚至下了赌注。乔西·派伊坚信吉尔伯特会胜出。安妮则担心自己失败的痛苦难以承受。

paragraphs.en: Anne eagerly awaited the pass list for her exams, driven by a desire to excel not just for herself but also for Matthew and Marilla. She hoped to be among the top ten, so she could see Matthew's proud eyes light up with pride at her success. This thought filled her with joy despite the hard work and tedious study.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮急切地等待着成绩单，她不仅为了自己，还为了马修和玛丽拉而渴望取得优异的成绩。她希望能进入前十名，这样就能看到马修因她的成功而骄傲的目光。这个念头让她尽管经历了辛勤的努力和枯燥的学习，依然感到无比喜悦。

paragraphs.en: For two weeks, Anne and her friends Jane, Ruby, and Josie frequented the post office, anxiously checking the Charlottetown dailies for any news. Charlie and Gilbert joined them in their anxious wait, but Moody Spurgeon avoided the ordeal, saying he preferred to be told his fate rather than face it himself.
paragraphs.zh: 两周以来，安妮和她的朋友们简、ruby和乔西频繁光顾邮局，焦急地查看夏洛特镇的日报，希望能找到任何消息。查理和吉尔伯特也加入了她们焦虑的等待之中，但莫迪·斯普劳尔却避开了这场煎熬，表示宁愿被告知结果也不愿亲自面对。

paragraphs.en: Three weeks passed without the list appearing, and Anne began to feel overwhelmed by the tension. Her appetite waned, and she grew disinterested in Avonlea's affairs. Matthew noticed her pale and indifferent appearance and wondered if voting for the Liberals might be better next time.
paragraphs.zh: 三周过去了，选民名单依然没有公布，安妮开始感到压力山大。她的食欲减退了，对埃文利镇上的事情也提不起兴趣。马修注意到她脸色苍白、神情漠然，心想下次或许应该支持自由党了。

paragraphs.en: One evening, as Anne sat at her open window, enjoying the summer dusk, Diana arrived with a fluttering newspaper. The pink sky reflected from the pines caught Anne’s attention, but it was Diana’s arrival that brought the news she had been waiting for.
paragraphs.zh: 一个傍晚，安妮坐在敞开的窗前，享受着夏夜的余晖。戴安娜带着一张飘动的报纸 arrived 惊叫道。天边粉红色的晚霞映在松树上，吸引了安妮的目光，但真正让她兴奋的是戴安娜的到来，带来了她期盼已久的消息。

paragraphs.en: Anne stood up, knowing immediately that the paper held her fate. The pass list was out! Her heart raced, and she felt dizzy.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮站起身来，立刻明白那张纸将决定她的命运。放榜了！她的心跳加速，感到一阵眩晕。

paragraphs.en: She couldn't move; it seemed like an eternity before Diana burst into the room without knocking.
paragraphs.zh: 她动弹不得，似乎过了好一会儿，戴安娜才敲门而入。

paragraphs.en: "Anne, you've passed," Diana exclaimed, "passed first—tied with Gilbert—but your name is first. Oh, I'm so proud!"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，你通过了！”戴安娜脱口而出，“你是第一名——和吉尔伯特并列第一，但你的名字排在前面。哦，我太为你骄傲了！”

paragraphs.en: Diana threw the paper on the table and collapsed onto Anne's bed, breathless. Anne lit a lamp, fumbling for matches before finally managing to light it. She grabbed the paper; there was her name at the top of the list!
paragraphs.zh: 戴安娜喘着气把报纸扔在桌子上，瘫倒在安妮的床上。安妮点燃了一盏灯，摸索了好一会儿才终于点着了火。她拿起报纸；她的名字赫然排在名单首位！

paragraphs.en: That moment was worth living for.
paragraphs.zh: 那一刻，一切努力都变得值得。

paragraphs.en: "You did splendidly, Anne," Diana said, recovering enough to sit up. "Father brought the paper home from Bright River just ten minutes ago—it came on the afternoon train and won't arrive by mail until tomorrow. I rushed over like a wild thing when I saw your name."
paragraphs.zh: “你表现得棒极了，安妮，”戴安娜坐起身说道，“你父亲刚才从光明河站带回了那份名单——下午的火车才刚到，明天才能通过邮件送达。我一看到你的名字就迫不及待地跑过来了。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm dazzled inside," Anne replied. "I want to say so many things, but my words fail me. I never dreamed of this—yes, once!
paragraphs.zh: “我内心简直目不暇接，”安妮回答说，“我想说很多话，但就是说不出来。我从没想过会有这一天——是的，曾经有过一次！”

paragraphs.en: I let myself think 'What if I should come out first?' quakingly, for it seemed so vain and presumptuous. Diana, excuse me a moment.
paragraphs.zh: 我让自己想：“要是我能拔得头筹会怎么样？”心里不禁一阵战栗，觉得这未免有些自不量力。戴安娜，请你原谅我一下。

paragraphs.en: I must run to the field to tell Matthew. Then we'll go up the road and share the good news with everyone."
paragraphs.zh: 我得赶紧去田里告诉马修，然后我们再沿着小路把这个好消息告诉大家。

paragraphs.en: Anne rushed to the hayfield below the barn where Matthew was coiling hay, finding Mrs. Lynde talking with Marilla at the lane fence.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮飞奔到谷仓下面的草场，马修正在那里捆扎干草。她发现雷切尔·林德太太正和玛丽拉在小径栅栏旁交谈。

paragraphs.en: "Matthew," Anne exclaimed, "I passed and I'm first—or one of the first! I’m not vain, but I am thankful."
paragraphs.zh: “马修，”安妮脱口而出，“我通过了考试，而且是第一名——或者至少是前几名！我不是在自夸，但我确实感到非常感激。”

paragraphs.en: "Well now, I always said it," Matthew replied, gazing at the pass list happily. "I knew you could beat them all easy."
paragraphs.zh: “果然不出我所料，”马修望着那份录取名单高兴地说，“我知道你能轻松战胜他们所有人。”

paragraphs.en: "You've done pretty well, Anne," Marilla said, trying to hide her pride from Mrs. Rachel's critical eye.
paragraphs.zh: “你表现得不错，安妮，”玛丽拉说道，试图在雷切尔太太挑剔的目光下掩饰住自己的骄傲。

paragraphs.en: "I just guess she has done well," Marilla added heartily. "It’s a credit to your friends, Anne, and we're all proud of you."
paragraphs.zh: “我猜她表现不错，”玛丽拉热情地说，“这可是你朋友的荣耀，安妮，我们为你感到骄傲。”

paragraphs.en: That night, after talking with Mrs. Allan at the manse, Anne knelt by her open window under the moonlight. She murmured a prayer of gratitude and aspiration, filled with thankfulness for the past and reverence for the future. Her dreams that night were as fair and bright as maidenhood could desire.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，安妮在牧师家与艾伦太太交谈后，跪在月光下的窗前。她低声默念了一段感恩和希冀的祷告，心中充满了对过去的感激和对未来深深的敬畏。那一晚，她的梦如同少女所愿般美好而明亮。
